reading.body:
New York's only data center with a published power figure is a 3 MW CyrusOne colocation site, far below the 50 to 100 MW a single modern GPU cluster can draw.

The facility, NYM7 in Wappingers Falls, pairs that 3 MW with 100,000 square feet of technical space. That is a large building for a small electrical load, and it fits the profile of regional colocation rather than dense GPU hosting. Its SSAE 16 Type II certification points to audited enterprise workloads, the kind of tenant that values financial and operational controls over raw compute density.

The figure matters because power is what limits AI scaling, and New York publishes almost none of it. The state has 31 mapped data center locations, and this is the only one with a disclosed capacity number. So the single quantified piece of AI-relevant compute infrastructure in New York is a facility that cannot host a large training run or inference cluster on its own. That says as much about disclosure as it does about the state's actual portfolio.

What the data does not cover is the rest of that portfolio. There is no address, no nearest airport, and no announced expansion for this campus. Its suitability score of 46 out of 100 is computed from published IT capacity and operator type alone, with announced expansion listed as missing. The remaining mapped locations may include larger facilities that simply do not publish a megawatt figure, so the absence of a bigger number in New York is not evidence that none exists.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
